music.brief: Low steady pulse under a soft string pad, calm and focused, one gentle lift near the end, instrumental, for a short explainer video.

beats.text: It is not how many words your child hears that matters most.
beats.say: It is not how many words your child hears that matters most.

beats.text: It is how many conversations they have with you.
beats.sub: Here is the study behind that.
beats.say: It is how many conversations they have with you. Here is the study behind that.

beats.text: 36 children wore a small recorder for two days.
beats.sub: It counted every word they heard, and every back-and-forth with an adult.
beats.say: Thirty six children wore a small recorder for two days. It counted every word they heard, and every back and forth exchange with an adult.

beats.text: What predicted the children's language skills
beats.say: Those back and forth exchanges predicted the children's language skills better than the number of words they heard.

beats.text: Only the exchanges were linked to activity in the speech part of the brain.
beats.sub: Whatever the family's income or education.
beats.say: And only the exchanges were linked to activity in the part of the brain that handles speech, whatever the family's income or education.

beats.text: The honest catch: this was a small study.
beats.sub: But a later trial that coached families into more back-and-forth found the same thing.
beats.say: The honest catch is that this was a small study. But a later trial that coached families into more back and forth found the same thing.

beats.text: Ask your child a question, then wait for the answer.
beats.sub: Build on whatever they say, even one word about a truck.
beats.say: So ask your child a question, wait for the answer, and build on whatever they say, even one word about a truck.

beats.text: The full claim, with every source, is free.
beats.say: The full claim, with every source, is free on our site. The link is in the bio.
